''[[Lychnis]] coronaria'' (L.) Desr. }} '''''Silene coronaria''''', the '''rose campion''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to Eurasia. Other common names include '''dusty miller''' (which also refers to ''[[Centaurea cineraria]]'' and ''[[Jacobaea maritima]]''), '''mullein-pink''' and '''bloody William'''. In the United Kingdom it is still widely referenced under its [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Lychnis coronaria'''''. == Description == It is a [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|80|cm|0|abbr=off}} tall by {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide, with grey felted [[leaves]] and single, bright magenta flowers produced in succession around July. Though short-lived, the plant readily self-seeds in favourable locations. It is sometimes grown as a [[biennial plant|biennial]].{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}} == Etymology == The Latin ''coronaria'' means "used for garlands".{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for gardeners |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |year=2012 |isbn=9781845337315 |location=United Kingdom |pages=224}} == Cultivation == It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]],{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10602/Lychnis-coronaria/Details | title = ''Lychnis coronaria'' |website=www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 12 April 2020}} as has the white-flowered [[cultivar]] 'Alba'.{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/19807/Lychnis-coronaria-Alba/Details | title = ''Lychnis coronaria'' 'Alba' | publisher = RHS |website=www.rhs.org | access-date = 12 April 2020}} Lychnis coronaria J1.JPG Silene coronaria-001.jpg Lychnis coronaria C.jpg Lychnis coronaria MHNT.BOT.2007.40.71.jpg == Notes == {{Reflist}} == References == * Armitage, Allan M.
